title: How to make a product promo video without a designer
meta_title: Product Promo Video Without a Designer — Akdeinz Motion
description: Make a product promo video yourself with CapCut or Canva: steps, hours and a cost table, versus a €1,290 Product Promo delivered in 7 working days.
answer: You can make a basic 30-second product promo yourself in CapCut or Canva using phone footage, which takes roughly 6–15 hours for a first one. If you would rather not, Akdeinz Motion’s Product Promo (30–45 s) is €1,290 excl. VAT, delivered in 7 working days in 16:9, 9:16 and 1:1.

diy.intro: A simple promo needs one message, a few clean shots of the product and a clear call to action. Decide where it will run first (Instagram Reels, a product page, paid ads) because that sets the aspect ratio.

tools.name: CapCut
tools.note: Timeline editor with keyframes, captions and templates. A good fit for assembling phone footage into a vertical promo. Check commercial-use terms for templates and music.

tools.name: Canva
tools.note: Simple drag-and-drop video editor with brand kit and templates. Quick for text-led promos; less control over timing.

tools.name: Jitter
tools.note: Browser-based tool for animating product screenshots, UI or graphics into short clips.

tools.name: After Effects
tools.note: Maximum control for animated product graphics. Not realistic as a first tool for a one-off promo.

steps: Write the single sentence the video must get across, for example what the product does and for whom.
Make a short shot list: the product alone, the product in use, one close-up detail, and the logo.
Film on a phone in daylight, with a steady surface. Shoot vertical and keep extra space around the product so you can crop to 1:1 and 16:9.
Assemble the clips in CapCut or Canva. Open with the most interesting shot; do not start with the logo.
Add on-screen text for the main benefit and a call to action at the end. Many people watch without sound, so add captions.
Add music you have the right to use in a commercial video, then export in 9:16, 1:1 and 16:9.
diy.hours: Realistic time for a first 30-second promo: about 1–2 hours filming and 4–10 hours editing and exporting, so roughly 6–15 hours in total. Later promos go faster once you have a template.

sections.h2: A simple structure for a 30-second product promo
ul: 0–3 seconds: a hook, usually the problem or the most striking shot.
3–10 seconds: what the product is and the main benefit.
10–22 seconds: the product in use or the key features, one idea per shot.
22–30 seconds: proof or result if you have a real one, then the call to action and logo.

time_line: Making your first one: ~6–15 hours. Akdeinz: €1,290, 7 working days.

diy_fine.p: Doing it yourself is fine in these cases:
ul: You are testing whether a product sells and the promo is disposable.
You already have good footage and only need to cut it together with text.
The video runs organically on your own channels and is replaced every few weeks.
You have more time than budget and want to learn basic editing.
diy_fine.not_fine: Consider hiring when the promo will run as a paid ad for months, sits at the top of a product page, or when 6–15 hours of your week are worth more than the difference in price.

faq.q: How long should a product promo video be?
faq.a: Akdeinz Motion’s Product Promo is 30–45 seconds. Social ads are shorter: up to 15 s (€490) or up to 30 s (€790).

faq.q: Can I make a product video with only a phone?
faq.a: Yes. Good light, a steady surface and a clear message matter more than the camera. Assemble the clips in CapCut or Canva.

faq.q: What does a Product Promo cost?
